tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Spec: crew-profile

## Goal
Add the crew profile of build step 9 (`design/DESIGN.md:72`) to the API and the CLI. A crew member shows their profile, and lists and changes their own skills and unavailability. The API rejects a change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (`design/DESIGN.md:305-312`).

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Only crew members use the profile routes (DESIGN 335). | A director and a lead each get 403 on each `/profile` route. The body is `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Only crew members manage a profile"}`. A request without a token gets 401. |
| AC2 | A crew member shows their profile. | `GET /profile` gives 200 and exactly `{"username", "display_name", "org_name"}` of the caller. |
| AC3 | A crew member lists their own skills (DESIGN 12). | `GET /profile/skills` gives 200 and one item `{"skill_id", "skill_name", "level"}` for each own skill, sorted by skill name. It has no skill of another user. |
| AC4 | A crew member adds a skill or changes its level (DESIGN 12, 431). | `PUT /profile/skills/{skill_id} {"level": n}` gives 200 and the crew skill. A skill that is not in the profile is added. A skill in the profile gets the new level. `level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. |
| AC5 | A skill names only a skill of the own org (DESIGN 355). | `PUT` with a `skill_id` that does not exist, or that belongs to another org, gives 422 with `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`. Both cases give the same body. No row changes. |
| AC6 | A crew member removes a skill (DESIGN 12, 431). | `DELETE /profile/skills/{skill_id}` gives 204. The skill is not in `GET /profile/skills`. A skill that is not in the profile gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. |
| AC7 | A crew member lists their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `GET /profile/unavailability` gives 200 and each own entry, past and future, as `{"id", "start_date", "end_date", "reason"}`, sorted by `start_date`. It has no entry of another user. |
| AC8 | A crew member adds unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `POST /profile/unavailability {"start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` gives 201 and the entry. A one-day entry is valid. An entry that overlaps an own entry is valid. `end_date < start_date` gives 422. A missing or unknown `reason` gives 422. |
| AC9 | A crew member removes their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 178). | `DELETE /profile/unavailability/{id}` gives 204. An ID of another crew member of the own org, of another org, or a random UUID gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. The other entry does not change. |
| AC10 | The API rejects an entry that overlaps an active assignment (DESIGN 310). | An entry that overlaps the dates of a mission with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. An overlap of one day at either end counts. No row is added. A DECLINED or CANCELLED assignment does not block. |
| AC11 | The API rejects a level below the minimum of an active slot (DESIGN 311). | `PUT` with a level below `min_level` of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller with that skill gives 409. A level equal to `min_level` gives 200. The stored level does not change after a 409. |
| AC12 | The API rejects removal of a skill that an active slot requires (DESIGN 312). | `DELETE` of a skill that is the skill of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. The skill stays in the profile. |
| AC13 | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment blocks, for each mission status. | An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level. |
| AC14 | The 409 body names each conflict (DESIGN 306). | The body is `{"detail": "<lines>"}` with one line for each conflict, sorted by mission start date. A skill line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): slot <position> requires <skill> level <min_level>.` An entry line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): the mission runs <start_date> to <end_date>.` |
| AC15 | Profile data of another org is not visible (DESIGN req 4, 22). | A crew member of org B gets 422 on `PUT` and 404 on `DELETE` with a skill of org A. A crew member of org B gets 404 on `DELETE` of an entry of org A. The org A rows do not change. |
| AC16 | The CLI runs the profile commands (DESIGN 430-432). | `mc profile show`, `mc profile skills list\|set\|remove` and `mc profile availability list\|add\|remove` each call the API and show the result. `add` requires `--from`, `--to` and `--reason`. A 403, 404, 409 or 422 exits 1 with the API message and no traceback. |

## Non-goals
- Skills and unavailability in `mc profile show`. The list commands show them.
- The org crew view for directors and leads. It is build step 10 (`design/DESIGN.md:73`).
- A change of an existing unavailability entry. The crew member removes it and adds a new one.
- A check of own overlapping entries or of past dates.
- A mission status filter in the conflict check. An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level forever, unless a later step changes its status.
- A schema change or a migration. The `crew_skill` and `unavailability` tables of step 2 have all the columns.
- Short references for skills (P1, `design/DESIGN.md:82`).

## End-to-end check
| # | Action | Expected result | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `mc login --user ava`, then `mc profile show` | Exit 0. The output contains `ava`, `Ava Lindqvist` and `Artemis Space Agency`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 2 | `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0. The output has `Piloting` with level 5 and `Communications` with level 4. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 3 | `mc profile skills set <EVA id> --level 2`, then `mc profile skills set <Piloting id> --level 4`, then `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0 each. The list has `EVA` 2 and `Piloting` 4. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 4 | `mc profile skills remove <EVA id>`, then `mc profile skills list` | Exit 0 each. The list does not have `EVA`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 5 | `mc profile availability add --from 2027-03-01 --to 2027-03-05 --reason HOLIDAY`, then `mc profile availability list` | Exit 0 each. The add output has `Added unavailability <id>`. The list has the entry with `2027-03-01`, `2027-03-05` and `HOLIDAY`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 6 | `mc profile availability remove <id>`, then `mc profile availability list` | Exit 0 each. The list does not have the entry. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 7 | `mc login --user hana`, then `mc profile skills set <Robotics id> --level 2` | Exit 1. The output contains `Orbital Debris Survey`, `INVITED` and `Robotics level 3`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 8 | As hana, `mc profile availability add --from 2026-12-10 --to 2026-12-10 --reason SICK` | Exit 1. The output contains `Orbital Debris Survey` and `2026-12-07 to 2026-12-18`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 9 | `mc login --user nell` (org B), then `mc profile skills set <org A Medicine id> --level 3` | Exit 1. The output contains `Unknown skill`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |
| 10 | `mc login --user diana`, then `mc profile show` | Exit 1. The output contains `DIRECTOR` and `Only crew members manage a profile`. | `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` |

The E2E test uses the seed data and the `api_url` and `mc` fixtures of `packages/api/tests/e2e/conftest.py` (`.work/missions-draft/plan.md:121`). The skill IDs come from `mc skills list` (`.work/missions-draft/plan.md:179`).

## Resolved questions
| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Task name? | `crew-profile`, folder `.work/crew-profile/` | me |
| Which state does step 9 start from? | Step 4 is complete as `.work/missions-draft/plan.md` describes it. This includes `routers/`, `commands/`, `dependencies.require_roles`, `OrgScope.get(..., for_update=True)`, `GET /skills`, `mc skills list`, the 409 and 422 CLI messages and `e2e/conftest.py`. Steps 5 to 8 are not necessary. | me, `.work/missions-draft/plan.md:121,169-176,242,282,321` |
| Does step 9 include the org crew view of requirement 11? | No. DESIGN has a new build step 10 for it and a "Changes" section. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:73` |
| Which API paths? | `/profile`, `/profile/skills/{skill_id}`, `/profile/unavailability/{id}`. `/me` stays for all roles. | me |
| What does `GET /profile` return? | A new type `ProfileOut` with `username`, `display_name` and `org_name` only. Skills and unavailability have their own list routes, so the profile route does not load them. | me |
| Which roles use `/profile`? | Crew only. A router dependency gives 403 with the rule `Only crew members manage a profile` on each route. | me, `design/DESIGN.md:335` |
| Which assignments block a profile change? | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller, for each mission status | me, `design/DESIGN.md:306` |
| What is the 409 body? | A text `detail` with one line for each conflict. The step 4 CLI prints a 409 text `detail`. | me, `.work/missions-draft/plan.md:282` |
| How does the CLI set the reason? | `--reason HOLIDAY\|SICK\|MEETING` is required. The API requires the field too. | me, `packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py:121` |
| What does a crew member get for an entry of another crew member? | 404, the same as a missing ID | me |
| Which entries does the API accept? | Each range with `end_date >= start_date`. Own overlap and past dates are allowed. The conflict check still applies. | me |
| Which entries does the availability list show? | All own entries, sorted by `start_date` | me |
| How do profile writes and step 7 invites run at the same time? | Each profile write locks the caller row with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` before the conflict check. Step 7 locks the same row (DESIGN 303). | me, `design/DESIGN.md:303` |
| What do the write routes return? | Only the changed item. `PUT` skill gives 200 and the crew skill. `POST` entry gives 201 and the entry. Each `DELETE` gives 204. The CLI prints one line for each write. | me |
| What does `PUT` return for an unknown or cross-org skill? | 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`, as step 4 does for slots | me, `.work/missions-draft/spec.md` AC12 |
| Where do the checks live? | In `routers/profile.py`, as step 4 keeps its rules in its router | me, `.work/missions-draft/plan.md:324-327` |
| Does step 9 need a migration? | No. The tables have all the columns. | `packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py:95-123` |
| Which seed data proves the conflicts? | hana has Robotics 4 and an INVITED assignment on slot 2 (Robotics, level 3) of "Orbital Debris Survey", 2026-12-07 to 2026-12-18. ivan has an ACCEPTED assignment on the COMPLETED "Lunar Relay Repair", slot 1 Piloting level 3. | `packages/api/src/mc_api/seed.py:50-51,75-83` |

## Goal
Add the crew profile of build step 9 (`design/DESIGN.md:72`) to the API and the CLI. A crew member shows their profile, and lists and changes their own skills and unavailability. The API rejects a change that conflicts with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment (`design/DESIGN.md:305-312`).

## Acceptance criteria
| ID | Criterion | The tests must prove |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Only crew members use the profile routes (DESIGN 335). | A director and a lead each get 403 on each `/profile` route. The body is `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Only crew members manage a profile"}`. A request without a token gets 401. |
| AC2 | A crew member shows their profile. | `GET /profile` gives 200 and exactly `{"username", "display_name", "org_name"}` of the caller. |
| AC3 | A crew member lists their own skills (DESIGN 12). | `GET /profile/skills` gives 200 and one item `{"skill_id", "skill_name", "level"}` for each own skill, sorted by skill name. It has no skill of another user. |
| AC4 | A crew member adds a skill or changes its level (DESIGN 12, 431). | `PUT /profile/skills/{skill_id} {"level": n}` gives 200 and the crew skill. A skill that is not in the profile is added. A skill in the profile gets the new level. `level` outside 1 to 5 gives 422. |
| AC5 | A skill names only a skill of the own org (DESIGN 355). | `PUT` with a `skill_id` that does not exist, or that belongs to another org, gives 422 with `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <id>"}`. Both cases give the same body. No row changes. |
| AC6 | A crew member removes a skill (DESIGN 12, 431). | `DELETE /profile/skills/{skill_id}` gives 204. The skill is not in `GET /profile/skills`. A skill that is not in the profile gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. |
| AC7 | A crew member lists their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `GET /profile/unavailability` gives 200 and each own entry, past and future, as `{"id", "start_date", "end_date", "reason"}`, sorted by `start_date`. It has no entry of another user. |
| AC8 | A crew member adds unavailability (DESIGN 13, 432). | `POST /profile/unavailability {"start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` gives 201 and the entry. A one-day entry is valid. An entry that overlaps an own entry is valid. `end_date < start_date` gives 422. A missing or unknown `reason` gives 422. |
| AC9 | A crew member removes their own unavailability (DESIGN 13, 178). | `DELETE /profile/unavailability/{id}` gives 204. An ID of another crew member of the own org, of another org, or a random UUID gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. The other entry does not change. |
| AC10 | The API rejects an entry that overlaps an active assignment (DESIGN 310). | An entry that overlaps the dates of a mission with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. An overlap of one day at either end counts. No row is added. A DECLINED or CANCELLED assignment does not block. |
| AC11 | The API rejects a level below the minimum of an active slot (DESIGN 311). | `PUT` with a level below `min_level` of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller with that skill gives 409. A level equal to `min_level` gives 200. The stored level does not change after a 409. |
| AC12 | The API rejects removal of a skill that an active slot requires (DESIGN 312). | `DELETE` of a skill that is the skill of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. The skill stays in the profile. |
| AC13 | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment blocks, for each mission status. | An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level. |

Write in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: active voice, one instruction per sentence, 20 words or fewer per instruction, no filler.

You are the implementer for slice 3. The repo root is the working directory.

## Brief

The main session read the plan and the spec. This brief holds the parts that you need. Do not read the plan or the spec.

### Slice

### Slice 3: A crew member lists, adds and removes their own unavailability

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/shared/src/mc_shared/__init__.py`, `packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py:32-35`, `packages/api/src/mc_api/routers/profile.py`, `packages/cli/src/mc_cli/commands/profile.py`
- Test (test writer): `packages/api/tests/test_profile_unavailability.py`, `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py`

**Covers:** AC7, AC8, AC9, AC15 (unavailability), AC16 (`availability list`, `add`, `remove`)

**Tests must prove:** The list has all entries of the caller, past and future, sorted by start date. `POST` adds a valid entry, also a one-day entry and one that overlaps an own entry. A wrong range or reason gives 422. `DELETE` removes only an entry of the caller. An entry of another user or org gives 404 and does not change. Examples:
- integration: crew member X has entries 2027-05-01..2027-05-03 (SICK) and 2025-01-10..2025-01-12 (HOLIDAY). Crew member Y of the same org has one entry. X sends `GET /profile/unavailability` → 200. The body has 2 items, the 2025 entry first. Each item equals `{"id", "start_date", "end_date", "reason"}` of the row.
- integration: X sends `POST /profile/unavailability {"start_date": "2027-06-01", "end_date": "2027-06-01", "reason": "MEETING"}` → 201. The body has the new `id` and the same values.
- integration: X sends an entry 2027-05-02..2027-05-04 that overlaps the own SICK entry → 201.
- integration: `end_date` one day before `start_date` → 422. A missing `reason` → 422. `"reason": "VACATION"` → 422. (Review Focus 4) `"reason": "holiday"` → 422. No row is added in these cases.
- integration: X sends `DELETE /profile/unavailability/<own id>` → 204. The next `GET` does not have it.
- integration: X sends `DELETE` with the ID of the entry of Y → 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. With the ID of an entry of org B → 404. With `uuid4()` → 404. The entries of Y and org B still exist.
- integration (Review Focus 1): `DELETE /profile/unavailability/abc` → 422.
- integration: a lead sends `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE` → 403 with the role body.
- unit: `mc_api.models.UnavailabilityReason is mc_shared.UnavailabilityReason` → true. The `alembic check` test still passes.
- E2E (spec steps 5 and 6): in `test_crew_journey`, after step 4.
  - `mc profile availability add --from 2027-03-01 --to 2027-03-05 --reason HOLIDAY` → exit 0. The output matches `Added unavailability ([0-9a-f-]{36})`.
  - `mc profile availability list` → exit 0. The output has a row with that ID, `2027-03-01`, `2027-03-05` and `HOLIDAY`.
  - `mc profile availability remove <id>` → exit 0. The output contains `Removed unavailability <id>`. `mc profile availability list` → the output does not contain the ID.
- E2E (Review Focus 3): `mc profile availability add --from 2027-02-30 --to 2027-03-01 --reason SICK` → exit 1. The output contains `start_date` and no `Traceback`.
- E2E (Review Focus 4): `mc profile availability add --from 2027-03-01 --to 2027-03-02 --reason holiday` → exit 1. The output contains `reason` and no `Traceback`.
- E2E: `mc profile availability add --from 2027-03-01 --to 2027-03-02` (no `--reason`) → exit code not 0. The output names `--reason`.

**Checkpoint:** `.claude/hooks/verify.sh full` → exit 0, no `ERROR` line. `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py` ran and passed.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the profile router and `commands/profile.py` from slices 1 and 2. `Unavailability` (`packages/api/src/mc_api/models.py:100-115`). The `check_dates` validator pattern of `MissionCreate` (`packages/shared/src/mc_shared/__init__.py:71-75`).
- Produces:

  ```python
  # mc_shared
  class UnavailabilityReason(StrEnum): HOLIDAY; SICK; MEETING     # moved from mc_api.models
  class UnavailabilityCreate(BaseModel):
      start_date: date; end_date: date; reason: UnavailabilityReason   # model validator: end_date >= start_date
  class UnavailabilityOut(BaseModel):
      id: UUID; start_date: date; end_date: date; reason: UnavailabilityReason

  # mc_api.routers.profile
  # GET    /profile/unavailability                    -> list[UnavailabilityOut], sorted by start_date, then end_date
  # POST   /profile/unavailability (201)              -> UnavailabilityOut. Body: UnavailabilityCreate
  # DELETE /profile/unavailability/{unavailability_id} -> 204, no body

  # mc_cli.commands.profile
  availability = typer.Typer()   # added to profile app as "availability"; commands "list", "add", "remove"
  ```

  CLI output:
  - `mc profile availability list`: a Rich table with the columns `ID`, `From`, `To`, `Reason`. The ID column has `no_wrap=True`.
  - `mc profile availability add --from <date> --to <date> --reason <HOLIDAY|SICK|MEETING>`: all three options are required. Send the dates and the reason as text, so the API checks them. The help text names the 3 reasons. It prints `Added unavailability <id>`.
  - `mc profile availability remove <id>`: `Removed unavailability <id>`.

**Steps:**

- [ ] **Step 3 (implementer): Move `UnavailabilityReason`.** Define it in `mc_shared`. In `models.py`, delete the class and import it from `mc_shared`. The DB enum name stays `unavailability_reason`. `seed.py` and `test_schema.py` import it from `mc_api.models`, and that import still works. Run `uv run pytest packages/api/tests/test_migration.py packages/api/tests/test_schema.py -q`. Expected: PASS.
- [ ] **Step 4 (implementer): Add `UnavailabilityCreate` and `UnavailabilityOut`.**
- [ ] **Step 5 (implementer): Add the three unavailability routes.**
  - `GET`: `scope.select(Unavailability)` filtered by the caller.
  - `POST`: add the row with `org_id` and `user_id` from the caller. Commit. Return 201 and the entry.
  - `DELETE`: find the row through `scope.select(Unavailability)` by ID and caller. No row gives 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`. Do not use `scope.get`: it finds entries of other users of the same org. Delete, commit, return 204.
- [ ] **Step 6 (implementer): Add the `availability` sub-group** with `list`, `add` and `remove`.

### Global Constraints

- Do not change the schema. `alembic check` on `mc_test` must report no difference (`packages/api/tests/test_migration.py`).
- Put each request and response type in `mc_shared`. It depends only on Pydantic.
- Use absolute imports (`from mc_api.x import ...`), as in the codebase.
- The router reads and writes tenant data only through `OrgScope` (`scope.select`, `scope.get`, `scope.session`).
- Exact error bodies:
  - Director or lead on a `/profile` route: 403 `{"role": "<ROLE>", "rule": "Only crew members manage a profile"}`.
  - Unknown or cross-org skill on `PUT`: 422 `{"detail": "Unknown skill: <skill_id>"}`.
  - Skill not in the profile on `DELETE`, or an entry that is not the caller's: 404 `{"detail": "Not found"}`.
  - Conflict: 409 `{"detail": "<one line for each conflict, joined with \n>"}`. The line formats are in slice 4.
- Check order: 401, then the crew 403 (router dependency), then 404 or 422, then 409.
- Each write route commits. `get_session` does not commit (`packages/api/src/mc_api/db.py:27-29`).
- Add one info-level log line for each successful write and each rejection (404, 422, 409) in the profile router. Use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`. Log IDs, never a token.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

You are the implementer for slice 4. The repo root is the working directory.

## Brief

### Slice

### Slice 4: Profile writes that conflict with an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment give 409

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/api/src/mc_api/routers/profile.py`
- Test (test writer): `packages/api/tests/test_profile_conflicts.py`, `packages/api/tests/e2e/test_profile_cli.py`

**Tests must prove:** Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller blocks an overlapping entry, a level below the slot minimum and the removal of the slot skill, for each mission status. DECLINED and CANCELLED assignments do not block. A 409 changes no row. The body names each conflict, one line each, sorted by mission start date. Examples:
- integration setup: org A, lead L, crew member X with skill `Robotics` 4. Mission M "Orbit Fix" 2027-02-10..2027-02-20, slot 2 `Robotics` min level 3. Assignment of X on slot 2 with status INVITED.

- integration: X sends `PUT /profile/skills/<Robotics id> {"level": 2}` → 409. The body equals `{"detail": "Conflicts with your INVITED assignment on mission 'Orbit Fix' (<M id>): slot 2 requires Robotics level 3."}`. The stored level is still 4.

  ```python
  # mc_api.routers.profile
  def active_assignments(scope: OrgScope, user: AppUser) -> list[tuple[Assignment, Mission, MissionRequirement, str]]
      # Locks the caller row first: scope.get(AppUser, user.id, for_update=True).
      # Then returns each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller, with its mission, slot and
      # slot skill name, for each mission status, ordered by Mission.start_date.
  def reject_conflicts(lines: list[str], action: str) -> None
      # No lines: returns. Else: logs one info line, then raises HTTPException(409, "\n".join(lines)).
  ```

  Line formats (exact):
  - Skill: `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): slot <position> requires <skill name> level <min_level>.`
  - Entry: `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): the mission runs <start_date> to <end_date>.`

  Conflict rules:
  - Entry: the entry overlaps the mission when `entry.start_date <= mission.end_date` and `entry.end_date >= mission.start_date`.
  - `PUT` skill: the slot skill is this skill and `level < slot.min_level`.
  - `DELETE` skill: the slot skill is this skill.

| AC12 | The API rejects removal of a skill that an active slot requires (DESIGN 312). | `DELETE` of a skill that is the skill of a slot of an INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment of the caller gives 409. The skill stays in the profile. |
| AC13 | Each INVITED or ACCEPTED assignment blocks, for each mission status. | An ACCEPTED assignment on a COMPLETED mission blocks a lower level. |
| AC14 | The 409 body names each conflict (DESIGN 306). | The body is `{"detail": "<lines>"}` with one line for each conflict, sorted by mission start date. A skill line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): slot <position> requires <skill> level <min_level>.` An entry line is `Conflicts with your <STATUS> assignment on mission '<title>' (<mission_id>): the mission runs <start_date> to <end_date>.` |

an unavailability entry that overlaps the mission dates, a skill level
